According to the latest issue of the "Power On" newsletter, Apple is reportedly once considered adding a feature to its "Apple Upgrade" programme that would make the process of switching to a new iPhone virtually seamless: pre-transferring user data before the new device ships. However, this feature ultimately did not come to fruition.

The concept is simple: if users are regularly upgrading their devices through fixed monthly instalments, why not make the switch as convenient as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reports:

There are some obvious gaps here. First, your iCloud backup will be slightly out of date, as data can only be transferred at the moment of shipment — a few days after placing the order — unless you choose to pick up the device in person at a store.

In addition, there are obvious privacy concerns. That said, if you have always been using iCloud backup, it is not surprising that Apple has your data. But the average user may worry about how the data is transferred to the new phone, and whether anyone has handled it during the process.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a brand-new system called "Presto" across its retail stores, allowing staff to update software while the iPhone is still in its box. It is not hard to imagine extending this system in the future to support iCloud backup transfers, with no one touching your data throughout the process.

However, this feature ultimately did not make it to market — and this may actually be a good thing.
